long_description:
Doximity Dialer is a telehealth communication tool from Doximity, the largest professional medical network in the US with over 2 million healthcare professional members. The Dialer enables physicians to make HIPAA-compliant video and phone calls to patients while masking their personal phone numbers with their office number.

The platform is free for verified physicians, which has driven massive adoption—over 85% of US physicians use Doximity, and the Dialer is one of its most popular features. Patients don't need to download an app or create accounts to receive calls, reducing friction for telehealth adoption.

Doximity has expanded Dialer capabilities to include a free AI scribe feature (currently in beta) that transcribes visits and generates clinical notes. The platform also integrates with Epic Haiku, allowing physicians to initiate Dialer calls directly from the Epic mobile app.

Over 150 health systems have enterprise agreements with Doximity, though the basic Dialer functionality remains free for individual physicians. The platform is designed primarily for physician-to-patient communication rather than complex multi-specialty telehealth workflows—health systems with enterprise virtual care needs may need additional platforms alongside Doximity.

faqs.a: Yes, Doximity Dialer is free for verified physicians (MDs and DOs). The platform includes video visits, phone calls, and caller ID masking at no cost.

faqs.q: What is Doximity Dialer caller ID masking?
faqs.a: Caller ID masking allows physicians to call patients while displaying their office number instead of their personal cell phone, protecting physician privacy while maintaining professional communication.

faqs.q: Does Doximity have an AI scribe?
faqs.a: Yes, Doximity has launched a free AI scribe feature (currently in beta) that transcribes telehealth visits and generates clinical notes for physicians using Dialer.
Doximity Dialer is primarily designed for verified physicians (MDs and DOs). Non-physician clinicians have limited access and may need to use alternative telehealth platforms.
